title: ASIRT investigating death of a man in Grande Prairie RCMP custody
article: A 26-year-old man died in custody at the Grande Prairie RCMP detachment sometime between Sunday night and Monday morning.
The man, arrested for mischief Sunday afternoon, was discovered unresponsive in his cell Monday morning when an officer went to check on him and other prisoners around 7:45 a.m.
Emergency Medical Services (EMS) was called and attended the detachment, however, the man was pronounced deceased on scene at 7:53 a.m.
The man ended up in police custody when RCMP responded to a 9-1-1 call at 1:54 Sunday afternoon to assist EMS.
When RCMP arrived, members found the man acting erratically and was believed to be high.
The man refused treatment from medics and also refused a police offer request to be transported to another location.
He was arrested for mischief as he was alleged to be interfering with "the lawful enjoyment and use of the property."
The man was booked into the detachment cells where he was expected to remain until it was determined he had recovered enough to be safely released.

The provincial Director of Law Enforcement was called as soon as the RCMP were made aware of the incident and the Alberta Serious Response Team (ASIRT) was called to investigate the in-custody death and the surrounding circumstances.
ASIRT investigates all police interactions resulting in serious injury or death, as well as serious instances of police misconduct.
This is the third in-custody death ASIRT is investigating this year.
The RCMP is also conducting an internal review process and will RCMP training, policy, response and the actions of employees will all be examined.
The name of the deceased hasn't been released.
